column1: # Measured decode rates, one row per run. TAB-separated.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS: llm-fit prints a tokens/sec estimate for every model
# it ranks, and exactly ONE of those numbers has ever been checked against a
# stopwatch. `llm-fit validate` turns this file into the predicted-vs-measured
# table, so collecting the rest is an afternoon rather than a project.
#   1. Run the model. Record the DECODE rate the runtime reports (llama.cpp
#      prints "eval time ... tokens per second"), not the prompt/prefill rate.
#   2. Record what the machine actually had FREE, not what is installed —
#      `llm-fit detect` prints both, and free is what the arithmetic uses.
#   3. ram_bw_gbs is MEASURED memcpy bandwidth (`llm-fit detect` says
#      "(measured)" when it has one). A spec-sheet number here silently
#   4. Say what was going on in `note`. A machine that was swapping produces
#      a real number that means something different.
# Nothing here is estimated, interpolated or filled in from a review. A row is
# a stopwatch or it is not a row.

column14: 26 of 48 layers on the GPU, 22 on a Ryzen 3700X; swap was still draining, so this is a floor. Source of cpuGatherEfficiency in internal/fit/fit.go.
